about: The display presets (osdos-display-<id>.txt beside this file), in Settings → Screen → Display Output's order: read by the app (src/display/DisplayOutput.cpp, which has it built in), by the website's builder for OSD/OS Setup (scripts/build-site.py) and by the image's setup helper (osdos-setup, from /usr/lib/osdos/display-presets.json).

exitCode: the code osdos-stop (scripts/install.sh, STOP_HELPER) writes the preset on, then reboots: its place in DISPLAY_PRESETS, counted from kDisplayPresetFirst (src/util/ExitCodes.h); keep the two in step. kDisplayThenPowerOff more, it writes it and powers off.
launcherApi: the launcher whose osdos-stop knows the code; the preset is offered from it on.
boards: the Raspberry Pis that have the output (src/util/Board: pi3, pi4, pi5). keyboard false: not on a keyboard model (Pi 400, Pi 500) either.
help: the help line for the output under the cursor in Display Output's chooser, and for the one in force on its row: what it is for, its lines and rate, what its name leaves out.
warning: said as the preset is chosen. A mode with a horizontal frequency above a standard arcade monitor's 15 kHz is said before it is chosen, for a monitor that can't take it may be damaged by it.

HDMI on all three. Composite: the AV jack (Pi 3, Pi 4), the TV pads (Pi 5), none on a keyboard model; a Pi 5's on GPIO 4-11 too (vec-gpio-pi5). SCART RGB on the GPIO pins (DPI): 480i and 576i on all three, and on the Pi 4 and the Pi 3, whose DPI and interlace are the firmware's, alike, 240p and 288p should it not hold.

JAMMA: a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board in RGB-Pi's layout: the Pi 4's and the Pi 3's firmware DPI, their sound on GPIO 18 and 19; the Pi 5's kernel DPI, its sound on a USB card, which interlaces only with GPIO 1, the board's I2C. A JAMMA mode's name says its scan rate, as an arcade monitor takes 15, 25 or 31 kHz, or several, and its preset's resolution (dpi_timings'), which tells apart the modes of the same lines. The font has no ×.

The JAMMA board's other modes: 320 across (the games' own pixels), super resolutions 1920 across, PAL's 288 lines, interlaced 480 and 576 lines (not a Pi 5's), 480 of them 640 across too, square pixels on a 4:3 tube, and the 25 and 31 kHz monitors'. JAMMA 480i at 640 across has its code after the 31 kHz one's, osdos-stop's last: it is in the menu beside the other 480i.

presets.label: HDMI
presets.help: A TV or monitor on HDMI, at the resolution it asks for

presets.label: Composite NTSC
presets.help: A TV on the AV jack (Pi 3, Pi 4) or the TV pads (Pi 5), in NTSC: 480 lines at 60 Hz

presets.label: Composite PAL
presets.help: A TV on the AV jack (Pi 3, Pi 4) or the TV pads (Pi 5), in PAL: 576 lines at 50 Hz

presets.label: GPIO Composite NTSC
presets.help: Composite from the Pi 5's GPIO pins 4 to 11, in NTSC: 480 lines at 60 Hz

presets.label: GPIO Composite PAL
presets.help: Composite from the Pi 5's GPIO pins 4 to 11, in PAL: 576 lines at 50 Hz

presets.label: SCART RGB NTSC
presets.help: A SCART TV through a cable on the GPIO pins, in RGB: 480 lines interlaced at 60 Hz, as NTSC's

presets.label: SCART RGB PAL
presets.help: A SCART TV through a cable on the GPIO pins, in RGB: 576 lines interlaced at 50 Hz, as PAL's

presets.label: SCART RGB 240p
presets.help: A SCART TV through a cable on the GPIO pins, in RGB: 240 lines at 60 Hz, should 480i not hold steady

presets.label: SCART RGB 288p
presets.help: A SCART TV through a cable on the GPIO pins, in RGB: 288 lines at 50 Hz, should 576i not hold steady

presets.label: JAMMA 240p 15 kHz (720x240)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 240 lines, 720 pixels across

presets.label: JAMMA 240p 15 kHz (320x240)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 240 lines, the games' own 320 pixels across

presets.label: JAMMA 240p 15 kHz (1920x240)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 240 lines, a super resolution 1920 across

presets.label: JAMMA 288p 15 kHz (720x288)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: PAL's 288 lines, 720 pixels across

presets.label: JAMMA 288p 15 kHz (1920x288)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: PAL's 288 lines, a super resolution 1920 across

presets.label: JAMMA 480i 15 kHz (720x480)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 480 lines interlaced, 720 pixels across

presets.label: JAMMA 480i 15 kHz (640x480)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 480 lines interlaced, 640 across, square pixels on a 4:3 tube

presets.label: JAMMA 576i 15 kHz (720x576)
presets.help: A 15 kHz arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 576 lines interlaced, 720 pixels across

presets.label: JAMMA 25 kHz (496x384)
presets.help: A 25 kHz (medium resolution) or tri-sync arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 496x384
presets.warning: For a medium resolution (25 kHz) or tri-sync monitor only: too high a scan rate can damage a 15 kHz one.

presets.label: JAMMA 31 kHz (640x480)
presets.help: A 31 kHz (VGA) or tri-sync arcade monitor through a Raspberry Pi to JAMMA board: 640x480
presets.warning: For a 31 kHz (VGA) or tri-sync monitor only: too high a scan rate can damage a 15 kHz one.
